headline: Fire breaks out at Dhaka airport in garbage pile near Gate 8
summary: Two Fire Service units responded to the incident at Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport on Saturday night.
details: A fire broke out in a pile of garbage near Gate 8 of Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport in the capital on Saturday night.
The Fire Service control room received the report of the fire at 9:20 PM on July 25.
Upon arrival, firefighters found smoke but no direct evidence of active flames.
Two Fire Service units worked to bring the situation under control, and the fire is now extinguished.
No casualties or injuries were reported in the incident, and the situation at the airport has returned to normal.
caption:
Fire reported at Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport! Two units responded to a garbage pile blaze near Gate 8.

A fire broke out in a pile of garbage near Gate 8 of Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport in the capital on Saturday night.

The Fire Service control room received the report of the fire at 9:20 PM on July 25.

Upon arrival, firefighters found smoke but no direct evidence of active flames.

Two Fire Service units worked to bring the situation under control, and the fire is now extinguished.

No casualties or injuries were reported in the incident, and the situation at the airport has returned to normal.

headline_marked: Austerity drive: [[Police escorts withdrawn for 18 ministers]] in Dhaka
headline: Austerity drive: Police escorts withdrawn for 18 ministers in Dhaka
summary: The move aims to reduce state spending and address acute shortages of police personnel and vehicles.
details: The government has withdrawn police movement escorts from 18 ministers as part of an austerity drive and to address shortages of police personnel and vehicles.
The Dhaka Metropolitan Police (DMP) has already implemented the decision, limiting the facility to only 14 key persons, including the Prime Minister and Home Minister.
Prime Minister Tarique Rahman has also scaled back his own protocol, reducing his movement escort from four vehicles to two.
The 14 key persons retaining escorts include seven parliamentary office-holders such as the Speaker and Leader of the Opposition, and seven other high-ranking officials.
The withdrawal applies only to police movement escorts within Dhaka; ministers will continue to receive gunmen, house guards, and protection during official tours outside the capital.
A typical minister's movement escort consists of one sub-inspector, four constables, and a police pickup van, with all costs borne by the state.
Currently, 1,691 police personnel are deployed in Dhaka for the personal security and movement of VIPs, including ministers and other state officials.
caption:
Police escorts for 18 ministers have been withdrawn in Dhaka as part of a government austerity drive.

The government has withdrawn police movement escorts from 18 ministers as part of an austerity drive and to address shortages of police personnel and vehicles.

The Dhaka Metropolitan Police (DMP) has already implemented the decision, limiting the facility to only 14 key persons, including the Prime Minister and Home Minister.

Prime Minister Tarique Rahman has also scaled back his own protocol, reducing his movement escort from four vehicles to two.

The 14 key persons retaining escorts include seven parliamentary office-holders such as the Speaker and Leader of the Opposition, and seven other high-ranking officials.

The withdrawal applies only to police movement escorts within Dhaka; ministers will continue to receive gunmen, house guards, and protection during official tours outside the capital.

A typical minister's movement escort consists of one sub-inspector, four constables, and a police pickup van, with all costs borne by the state.

Currently, 1,691 police personnel are deployed in Dhaka for the personal security and movement of VIPs, including ministers and other state officials.
